annotation.title_clean: Wyoming Enrolled Act No. 32 (HB0102): Artificial Intelligence Offenses and Developer Liability
annotation.title_en: Wyoming Enrolled Act No. 32 (HB0102): Artificial Intelligence Offenses and Developer Liability
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Wyoming State Legislature (Sixty-Eighth Legislature, 2026 Budget Session)
annotation.summary_en: Wyoming's 2026 enrolled act (HB0102) amends the criminal code to bar AI use as a defense to crime. It creates offenses for nonconsensual synthetic sexual material, AI child pornography and AI systems built to promote self-harm. It also gives developers conditional civil immunity and defines "artificial intelligence system". Effective July 1, 2026.
key_provisions_or_claims: Using an AI system to commit a crime is not a defense to criminal charges (W.S. 6-1-206).
Criminalizes distributing nonconsensual synthetic sexual material; felony up to 10-12 years.
Criminalizes developing or distributing AI systems designed for child pornography or to promote self-harm; felony up to 10 years.
AI developers are immune from damages for third-party misuse unless the system's primary purpose is illicit.
Adds a statutory definition of 'artificial intelligence system'; effective July 1, 2026.
